newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rebound after Japan eases fears of Treasury sales.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rebound after Japan eases fears of Treasury sales.

text.p: The stock market rose sharply in early trading Tuesday, recovering from the previous day's steep loss after Japan backed away from a warning that it might sell U.S. Treasuries.

Shortly after 10:00 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 64.46 points at 7,668.72 following Monday's 192-point plunge. The drop was second only to the 508-point drop when the market tumbled on Oct. 19, 1987.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, responding to a question after a speech Monday at Columbia University in New York, said that Japan had been tempted in the past to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities and boost its gold reserves, but had not done so.
Wall Street viewed the comment as a veiled threat by Hashimoto to sell off Japan's U.S. Treasury holdings.
But Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said, "The prime minister's real intention was not correctly reported" and that Japan had no intention of selling U.S. Treasuries.
A senior ministry official also told reporters that U.S. Treasuries were an essential part of Japan's foreign reserves.
Analysts said the stock market had over-reacted to Hashimoto's comments.
"A lot of yesterday's sell-off was not warranted," said Ron Doran, director of institutional trading at C.L. King and Associates.
Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood, said Monday's market plunge was an example of irrational panic caused by profit-taking.
Stocks have been vunerable to heavy selling pressure after soaring more than 20 percent since the start of the year amid a magic combination of steady economic growth and subdued inflation.

The recent strength, which pushed the Dow index to a record closing high of 7,796.51 on Friday, was also fuelled by expectations that the Federal Reserve would hold the line on interest rates at its July 1-2 policy meeting.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 9.11 points at 1,443.43.
The bond market also rebounded. The 30-year Treasury was up 6/32, trimming its yield to 6.69 percent from 6.70 percent on Monday.
